Updated main Python file with the last version of the framework (Every node can also mine every other node's blocks including request blocks [when the same node tries to mine both request and response transaction's blocks, it doesn't work properly. Other than that when two transactions are sent without being separately mined, there's a delay with the mining process. fix those!])

Updated main Python file with the last version of the framework (Every node can also mine every other node's blocks including request blocks [All the problems regarding this logic is fixed]. Also implemented the logic of erasing the mined transactions instead of storing them with the parameter 'status'.)

Updated main Python file with the last version of the framework (Every node can also mine every other node's blocks including request blocks [All the problems regarding this logic is actually NOW fixed]. Just an important thing, as the nodes get registered to each other in the very beginning, they should also register THEMSELVES!)

Added a new script, launch_nodes, to have the launch and the registration of the nodes automated, depending on the input. For now registration logic is not properly implemented, but the nodes get launched with the newly added script.
Added a new script, launch_nodes, to have the launch and the registration of the nodes automated, depending on the input. Registration logic is now implemented.
Upgraded the script, launch_nodes, to have a simple interactive menu and automated transaction creation, depending on the input.

Added new fields 'parent' (for response transactions) and 'hash' for transactions, to simplify the verification process. Added a method to verify request-response transactions' correctness using the newly added fields. For now it's only checking for one specific request transaction that's given (hash of it).

Added a new verification script for the request transactions, to check if they work without problems, reduced redundancy in the FlaskBlockChain.py and added additional methods in the launch_nodes.py to make sure that the nodes are correctly terminated afterwards.

Merged the verification script and the launch script together (to launch_nodes.py), added extra logic in FlaskBlockChain.py if the node would be a coordinator node. Clicking on "Trigger Verification" in the menu after running launch_nodes.py, a random coordinator node is going to be chosen and a random uneven amount of nodes is going to be chosen to verify the transactions in the last block. Depending on the votes of the verifier nodes, the coordinator is going to decide if the transactions in the last block are valid or not

Edited the launch_nodes.py script for a better terminal UI menu, added "Mine a Block", "Display the Blockchain" and "Show transaction pool" options to the menu. Also added a new getter endpoint for the FlaskBlockChain.py for the transaction pool.

Edited the initial launch and successfully registered message, checking if they are successfully registered and then print it in a single line for the UI, instead of multiple lines.
Timestamp format changed, to date and time (hh:mm)
Added an another option to the Menu, Inspect a specific block, the details about the block with the given number gets displayed.
Fixed the menu, added an extended version of menu for the display functions. Added a new "Show running nodes" function.
Added the new logic, "verification" transactions for the verification process, but right now coordinator doesn't check if the results match / are correct

Created a different version of verification, this time directly in the resolve_conflicts method for every time a response transaction is being mined.
Added a new transaction type, "verification", and it helps us to see if the first transaction of the blocks filled with response transactions are correct.
